correctness.rationale: The known uniform-triangle halfspace depth is D=4min(αβ,βγ,γα) for nonnegative barycentric coordinates with sum one. In chamber α≥β≥γ, the minimum is βγ and central set reduces to β≥max(γ,q/γ) and β≤(1−γ)/2, q=τ/4. The two ranges γ∈[r,√q] and [√q,1/3], r=(1−√(1−8q))/2, yield I=∫((1−γ)/2−q/γ)+∫((1−3γ)/2). Six chambers and simplex coordinate area 1/2 give normalized F=12I; independently symbolically integrated and evaluated at five interior levels, recovering F=(3/2)√(1−2τ)−1/2+(3τ/2)log[2(1−√(1−2τ))/(1+√(1−2τ))]. Endpoint max depth 4/9 follows pair-product maximum only at α=β=γ=1/3; F(0)=1, F(4/9)=0. Independent symbolic series for wet part is (3τ/2)log(1/τ)+(3τ/2)−(3τ²/4)+O(τ³). Known pointwise depth is a premise, not new. The Monte Carlo method in verify.py is corroborative and not infinite proof.
residual_risks: Exact only in plane for triangles with uniform area measure; not arbitrary polygons or higher dimensions. The core chamber integral is elementary given the prior depth formula.
